reasoning:
First, we extract the data from the stem-and-leaf plot. There are $n = 24$ data points. 
1. Minimum = 40, Maximum = 95.
2. Lower Quartile ($Q_1$): Average of the 6th and 7th values. Both are 44, so $Q_1 = 44$.
3. Median ($Q_2$): Average of the 12th and 13th values. Both are 52, so Median = 52.
4. Upper Quartile ($Q_3$): Average of the 18th and 19th values. Both are 65, so $Q_3 = 65$.

Now we look at the lengths on the box plot:
- Left whisker: $Q_1 - \text{Min} = 44 - 40 = 4$
- Box: $Q_3 - Q_1 = 65 - 44 = 21$. Within the box, the median (52) is 8 units from $Q_1$ and 13 units from $Q_3$, meaning it is closer to the left side of the box.
- Right whisker: $\text{Max} - Q_3 = 95 - 65 = 30$

Comparing these features: the distribution has a very short left whisker and a very long right whisker (positive skew), and the box is positioned towards the left side of the entire range. Only box plot D matches these characteristics.
